source.source_title: Make Art Feel Better with Billie Bivins: Whittling Wood
source.why_this_clip: An acoustic guitar leans against a chair, seen from the front with the neck rising up and to the right. The guitar itself is still; from 6.5 s the camera tilts and pans so the guitar slides down and right in frame. The clip has no cuts, and this interval keeps the whole body in frame while the camera move happens; after 8.0 s the body leaves the bottom of the frame.

camera.source: shots/guitar-sam/camera.json: phase correlation of the footage with the guitar masked out. The move is a downward tilt with a little pan, so the room behind the guitar slides almost exactly as far as the guitar does (86 px against the guitar's 89 px).

planes.label: Chair, legs and rug behind the guitar. Depth Anything puts them farther than the guitar (0.52 against 0.81), but the camera turns rather than travels, so the measured shift of the room is used almost as it is; a plane at the depth ratio would slide a third too slowly.
